title: Recursive Transaction Chain
scenario: Transactions are linked if an 'amount' from one transaction is moved to another. Find the full chain of transactions for a specific starting ID. Return the result table as 'id', 'amount', and 'depth'.
tableSchema: transactions (id INT, parent_id INT, amount INT, trans_date DATE)
hint: Use a Recursive CTE to traverse the parent_id to id link.
correctQuery: WITH RECURSIVE chain AS (SELECT id, parent_id, amount, 1 AS depth FROM transactions WHERE parent_id IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT t.id, t.parent_id, t.amount, c.depth + 1 FROM transactions t JOIN chain c ON t.parent_id = c.id) SELECT id, amount, depth FROM chain;
setupSQL: CREATE TABLE transactions (id INT, parent_id INT, amount INT, trans_date DATE); INSERT INTO transactions VALUES (1, NULL, 1000, '2026-01-01'), (2, 1, 500, '2026-01-02'), (3, 2, 250, '2026-01-03');
